comment: Northwest Caucasian, vigesimal from forty, and fifty is a half-hundred. Breton, Welsh and Garifuna do the same thing with no possible shared inheritance.
Generated from Unicode's own spellout rules. Sits a fraction below Dutch, which is about right for a daughter language with its own lexicon.

Vigesimal with subtraction at every odd ten. Thirty is ten-from-forty, fifty is ten-from-sixty. Because the score word appears in every number above twenty, this is one of the few real languages the base layer detects.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Niger-Congo.
Ge'ez script, tens before units. Pairs with Maltese as the two Semitic poles.
Sorted in Arabic's own alphabetical order with no special handling, and it comes out little-endian, exactly as the word order predicts. Masculine forms; the feminine set inverts.
The same numbers transliterated. Vowels appear that the Arabic script omits, and the regularity index rises by about a tenth. That gap is the abjad boundary.
The digits you already use, sorted as strings. Every number from ten to ninety-nine is two characters, so alphabetical order and numerical order coincide exactly.
Second widest decimal margin. Above ninety-nine it borrows from Quechua, but one to ninety-nine is entirely native.
Same numbers as Quechua. Two unrelated Andean families, one architecture.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Turkic.
As Russian, with vowel reduction in the spelling.
Literary forms. CLDR uses the contracted colloquial ones, which is a real difference rather than an error on either side.
The subtractive un- band runs one decade longer than in Hindi.
Verified against a linguistics olympiad problem, which is a better source than most because the arithmetic has to work for the puzzle to be solvable.
An isolate in the Karakoram. The teens use a different word for ten from the one the other decades use.
Vint-i-un rather than vint-i-u. Both attested.

Three source languages for the units: Arawak for one and two, Carib for three, French from four up. It carries a French vigesimal system more conservative than modern French, with forty as two twenties and sixty as three. The measure calls it decimal anyway, because the borrowed French teens are nine unanalysable words that wreck the first score.

Nineteen has its own word, unrelated to the pattern used for eleven through eighteen, and it costs nothing. Decade one was already built differently from every other decade, so a second irregularity inside it adds nothing the measure can see.
The same numbers in Latin letters. Divergence of about 0.01 from the syllabary, which is the price of a lossless change in granularity.
Cherokee syllabary. Sorted by codepoint.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Iroquoian.

An early build had the vowel elision applying across the whole twenties. The rule elides only before vowel-initial units. Correcting it moved the indices by 0.0001, which is the useful part of the story.
Colloquial Czech is little-endian where the standard is big-endian. One language, two registers, opposite signs.
Standard Czech puts the ten first. The colloquial register does the opposite.
A perfect score, and only after the soft mutation was added. Dau ddeg, not dau deg. That error was costing Welsh 0.03.

Lowest regularity in the corpus at 0.465. Vigesimal with a fifteen tier, four composition patterns, and mutations. Synthetic vigesimal languages with a fifteen tier built specifically to imitate it, four thousand of them, none came close. Whatever traditional Welsh is doing, no base model reproduces it.
The same system with the fifties built on forty rather than on half-a-hundred. Both are attested and the gap between them is about 0.09, which is the honest uncertainty band.

Halvtreds is two and a half twenties, with a subtractive fraction buried in it. Arithmetically the strangest number word in Europe. The measure does not care, because it is still one word in a consistent slot.

The mirror of English. Einundzwanzig puts the unit first, so the clusters group numbers ending in one rather than numbers in the twenties. Same structure, invisible on the plot. Germany, Austria and Switzerland write 1-99 the same, apart from the Swiss spelling dreissig, so one variant covers all three.

Strokes and cattle hobbles, repeated. The Unicode block follows Gardiner's sign list, and the hobble sorts before the stroke, so the whole sequence runs backwards. The only strongly negative rank correlation in the corpus.
Demotic forms. CLDR prefers katharevousa, so the two disagree on sixty-four of ninety without either being wrong.

Two odd teens, eleven and twelve, and that is the whole cost. Everything else is a clean tens-plus-units join. British, American and Australian English share these words 1-99, so one variant covers them all.
The calibration language. Its score has to be exactly one on ten to ninety-nine or the pipeline is broken.
Regular Romance. Numerals 1-99 are identical across Spain and all of Latin America, so American Spanish adds no new structure.
See Finnish. The pair is a coincidence forced by both being regular, not an independent confirmation of anything.
Chan calls it vigesimal and so does the sign of the base margin. The significance test does not agree, which is a fact about the test rather than about Basque.
Tens first, where Arabic puts units first. Two languages, one script, opposite signs.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Niger-Congo.
Identical architecture to Estonian with a different vocabulary. The two return the same numbers to four decimals, which says more about the measure than about Finnic.
Septante and nonante, quatre-vingts kept. Also standard in Switzerland, the DRC, Rwanda, Burundi and parts of eastern France, so the Belgian label is too narrow.
Huitante for eighty, mainly in Vaud, Valais and Fribourg. That single word flips the base verdict. Nothing else in the corpus turns on one lexical item this cleanly.
Geneva keeps septante but says quatre-vingts. A third point on a gradient that has four.

Regularity of 0.945, which looks respectable. Coherence of 0.625, which does not. The seventies borrow the teen words, so two decades out of nine draw their units from a different vocabulary. Only the coherence index noticed.
Modern Irish is decimal. The traditional vigesimal system is barely used now except daichead for forty.
Upper Brittany, in contact with Breton, and decimal anyway. A useful negative result for anyone reaching for a contact explanation of French seventy to ninety-nine.
Modern Scottish Gaelic, decimal.
Traditional vigesimal. Three forms are attested for twenty-one to twenty-nine and one was chosen.
Regular.
Po means hand and means five. The only language where a base-five grid comes close to tying with base ten.
The word order reverses at sixty. The first build had it uniform and was simply wrong. Manx is one of three variants whose endianness cannot be distinguished from zero.
The decimal variant, unverified.

Iwakalua for twenty breaks the pattern every other decade follows, and swapping it for a regular form changes the regularity index by nothing. That counterfactual is where the index revealed what it actually measures.
Units before tens, the reverse of the modern language.

The alphabet is the numeration, so the sort is almost the number line. Only seven of ninety sit off the diagonal, because fifteen and sixteen are written nine-plus-six and nine-plus-seven to avoid spelling the divine name.
Masculine forms. CLDR uses feminine, which is a genuine choice rather than a discrepancy.
Every compound is fused beyond analysis. The endianness reads negative not because Hindi is little-endian but because the unit prefix survived erosion while the tens marker did not.
Twenty is nees nkaum, unrelated to two or to ten, and ninety uses a different tens word from thirty through eighty. Two irregularities in the tens series, both free.
Ten, then a word meaning and, then the unit in its object form, then a word meaning additional. Four elements per number and a perfect score.
The connector was missing from seventy-two of ninety forms. Fixing it changed the indices by nothing at all.
Huszonegy, not húszegy. The tens stem changes before a unit and it costs nothing.
Perfect score. Armenian also has an alphabetic numeral system that is not built here.
Differs from Malay in exactly one word. Endianness and regularity identical to five decimals, base margin shifted by 0.056.
Forty is two twenties, sixty is three, eighty is four, and above twenty the remainders are the teen words. Thirty-five is literally twenty fifteen.
Conservative Germanic, no surprises.
Regular.
One of three Japanese notations. All ninety rank positions differ between them and every index is identical.
See kana.
See kana.
Jersey Norman has septante and nonante like Switzerland, plus huitante as an option. A Channel Island preserving what Paris lost.
The same variety with quatre-vingts instead. Both forms are listed side by side in the source, and they land on opposite sides of the base verdict. A within-variety flip on one word.
Four irregular zones: the teens, the twenties with their own suffix, and two opaque tens. Confirmed by five sources after a first attempt missed the twenties entirely.
Verified against Boeder and Hewitt through a secondary source. Rule and five worked examples matched on the first try.

Base-twenty positional digits invented by schoolchildren in Kaktovik, Alaska in 1994 and encoded in Unicode in 2022. On a one to ninety-nine window the measure calls it decimal. On ten to ninety-nine it gets it right. That is the argument for the narrower window.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Turkic.

Plotted hollow. The forms above twelve are historical; Greenlanders use Danish numbers today. The overcounting system it preserves names the block being entered rather than the one completed, so thirty is on the second person, ten.
Quinary units, an opaque twenty, and borrowed tens. One source claimed a connector in the compounds; three others show plain juxtaposition, and those three won.
Eight completely opaque tens, none derived from its units. Sixty is yesun, unrelated to yeoseot. Also a perfect score, and zero lexical overlap with the Sino set.
Perfect score.
The particle changes partway up the range, from warn ugens to ha. That switch is what costs it.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Turkic.
The additive variant, also attested. Isolates exactly what the subtraction costs.
Duodeviginti, undeviginti, duodetriginta. Two positions in every decade run backwards. Changing only eighteen of ninety numbers drops the endianness index from +0.82 to +0.04.
The most baroque join rule in the corpus. Three different patterns depending on decade and unit, all faithfully implemented, all free.
Wikcemna nunpa is ten two for twenty, with the multiplier after the base. The teens drop the base word entirely, which is what costs it.
As Thai.
Baltic, regular.
Baltic, regular.

Base sixty. Seventy, eighty and ninety are sixty plus ten, twenty, thirty. The measure ranks base ten first and base sixty second to last, because a window that stops at ninety-nine catches the sixty boundary exactly once.
Austronesian, unit before ten, and it needed no correction.
The widest decimal margin here. Every compound is three words plus a connector, so the decimal boundaries are spelled out and a base-twenty grid has nothing to grip.
Matches Bulgarian to four decimals. Same architecture.
Tens have a standalone form and a combining form. Arav becomes arvan before a unit.

Fewer than a hundred native speakers and perfectly documented, because the Qing archives are enormous. Fifteen is tofohon, the only suppletive form, and replacing it with a regular one lifts the score to exactly one. Four opaque tens cost nothing; one odd teen costs 0.022.

coord_source: manual correction (row previously held Malayalam coords)
comment: Differs from Indonesian in exactly one word.
The only language in the entire verification programme that needed no change at all. Semitic, Latin script, unit before ten.
The tone shift on the tens word is free. What costs is that ten keeps its multiplier and eleven drops it.
Clicks are Unicode letters and sort without incident. Perfect score, which is worth knowing: an alien phoneme inventory produces the same two numbers as Māori.
Little-endian like German, and slightly tidier. Identical in the Netherlands and Belgian Flemish, so one Dutch variant suffices.
The 1951 reform in action. Compare with the traditional variant, which runs the other way.
Pre-1951 Norwegian counted units first. The reform flipped the sign of the endianness index inside one lifetime.

coord_source: Wikipedia Ndom language / Yos Sudarso Island
comment: Base six, the only one here. Roots for six, eighteen and thirty-six, with multiplication and addition. The measure ranks base eighteen first and base six second, because tondor is the word that repeats most. Second lowest regularity in the corpus.
The twenties fuse and everything above is phrasal. Nine differently eroded teens are what costs it.
Regular.
Twenty uses a different suffix from thirty through ninety, and that is free. The teens optionally drop the base word, and that is not.
Spaced compounds. Slovak writes the same structure solid, which is why their base margins differ without any real difference in the language.
European (Portugal) forms, also used in Angola. Brazil differs only at 16, 17 and 19 - see pt-br.
The possessive suffix alternates on a phonological condition and it is free.

A textbook pure vigesimal system. Score words for twenty, forty, sixty and eighty, then a remainder from zero to nineteen. The measure gives it a base margin of minus 0.015, which is almost nothing. Because the scores are single words rather than repeated, there is no twenty to see in the string.
A linking vowel was inserted in every decade. It belongs only in the twenties, and only before consonants. Sixty-three wrong forms, eight thousandths of movement.
Contracted forms. Uncontracted alternatives exist and CLDR uses them.
Regular, big-endian, Cyrillic.
The units were Italianised in the first version. Logudorese has sete, oto, noe. Correcting them changed nothing numerically and everything about whether the data is right.
One of four Italo-Romance varieties here. They span 0.015 in endianness, which bounds how much dialectal variation the measure responds to.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Uralic.
Solid compounds. Reads as more decimal than Polish or Czech partly because of the spacing convention, not the morphology.
Little-endian. CLDR's own rule set returns a non-word for eighteen here, a reminder that Unicode is a strong source rather than an infallible one.
Regular.
Same as Croatian in structure, different script, identical numbers. A clean demonstration that the measure is script-blind.
Generated directly from Unicode CLDR spellout rules. Austronesian.
Plotted hollow. Only the units, the tens to fifty, sixty, and a single compound are attested. Everything else is reconstruction.
Unremarkable, which is the point of having it.
Roughly half the numeral vocabulary is borrowed from Arabic and the architecture is untouched. Perfect score.

Regularity of 0.996, which looks flawless. Coherence of 0.704, which puts it in the same class as French. Something changes construction between decades and only one index found it. What it is remains open.
Dravidian pair with Tamil. The near-identical numbers follow from both being regular.
Perfect, with one wrinkle at twenty and one at every x1 that costs nothing.
The tens suffix alternates by whether the root ends in a vowel. That looked expensive and turns out to be free, because it is phonologically conditioned.

A hundred and twenty-odd words in the whole language and no multiplication in the numerals. Ninety-nine is nine morphemes of pure repetition. Repetition turns out to be legible to the measure, which was not the expectation.
For a long time the widest decimal margin in the corpus. Agglutination costs nothing when it is positionally consistent.
As Russian.
Fusion plus an abjad. Both effects compound and it lands among the least regular. Real ICU collation made the result stronger rather than weaker.
Dash-joined compounds where Sicilian writes solid and Ligurian uses an apostrophe. Three orthographies, one morphology, near-identical numbers.
Three substitutions in the units position, all positionally consistent, all free.
Quinary in both units and tens, and the measure sees none of it.
Little-endian, Hebrew script, Germanic lexicon.
Units five through nine subtract from the next decade, and the odd decades subtract ten from the next even one, the same trick Danish uses. The base-five score of 0.191 is the lowest in the corpus.
Cantonese romanisation.
The strongest vigesimal reading of any spoken language here, and the reason is visible. Zapotec spells the multiplication out, so gande appears in every number from forty upward.
The anti-fraud forms used on cheques. Different characters, same structure.
Perfect. Sorted by codepoint.
Romanised. Same indices.
Radical order.
Stroke-count order.
Brazilian forms: dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove. Structure identical to European Portuguese; catorze kept.
CLDR RBNF spellout (Unicode), ICU-ranked. Little-endian and fused like its Indic neighbours; each 20-99 form is a portmanteau, not predictable from its parts.
ICU CLDR RBNF spellout, ICU-collated. Big-endian (tens-first). Coherence computed.

Constructed language (Johann Martin Schleyer, 1879). Perfectly regular decimal: teldeg = two-ten (20), degbal = ten-one (11), zueldegzuel (99).
